title: Same Words, Different Judgments: How Preferences Vary Across Modalities
abstract: arXiv:2602.22710v4 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Preference-based reinforcement learning (PbRL) is the dominant framework for aligning AI systems to human preferences. However, evaluation protocols for such data were designed for text and have not been validated for speech. We present the first intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC)-based, controlled cross-modal study of human and synthetic preference annotations, comparing text and audio evaluations of identical semantic content across 100 prompts. We show that achieving \textit{good} (audio) to \textit{near good} (text) agreement within either modality (ICC(2,$k$) $\approx$ .81 audio, .74 text) requires $\sim$9 raters and modalities show marked differences in how people report preferences: audio raters exhibit narrower decision thresholds, reduced length bias, and more user-oriented evaluation criteria, with near-chance cross-modality agreement. translated_title: 相同的话语，不同的评判：偏好如何随模态而变化
translated_abstract: 基于偏好的强化学习（PbRL）是将AI系统与人类偏好对齐的主流框架。然而，针对此类偏好数据的评估协议是为文本设计的，尚未在语音模态上得到验证。我们开展了首个基于组内相关系数（ICC）的、受控的跨模态研究，对人类与合成的偏好标注进行分析，在100个提示上比较了对相同语义内容的文本评估与音频评估。我们表明，在任一模态内部达到“良好”（音频）至“接近良好”（文本）的一致性水平（ICC(2,k) 音频约为 .81，文本约为 .74）需要约9名评分者；并且两种模态在人们报告偏好的方式上存在显著差异：音频评分者表现出更窄的决策阈值、更弱的长度偏差以及更偏向用户的评估标准，而跨模态的一致性接近随机水平。我们证明合成评分可以被用来有效预测……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该研究首次通过基于ICC的受控跨模态实验证明，人类在音频与文本两种模态下表达偏好的方式存在显著差异（跨模态一致性接近随机水平），因此原本为文本设计的偏好评估协议不能直接套用于语音模态。
en_tdlr: Through the first ICC-based controlled cross-modal study, this paper shows that humans report preferences markedly differently in audio versus text modalities—with near-chance cross-modal agreement—implying that evaluation protocols designed for text cannot be directly applied to speech.
